alt: Video by Roberto P. Nickson on September 16, 2026.

caption:
Anthropic just launched Fable 5.1 and in short: it’s faster, smarter, cheaper… and finally responds to you like a sane, normal person would.

More specifics:

- Solves agentic coding tasks at roughly half the cost of Fable 5
- Much faster and slightly more capable than Opus 5, and uses around half of the tokens
- Writing style is more natural
- Much more powerful at scientific research

I chat with people in my day-to-day life all of the time who think AI is useless… and when I dig a little deeper I realize they are using base/commodity/legacy models.

So if you haven’t taken the time to seriously test-drive a frontier model over the last few months, this is a good opportunity to do so. They have gotten extremely proficient and I think it’s important for people to understand their capabilities.

The last few months specifically have been a real step-change, and I anticipate the next wave of models to close out the years will be another major step as well.

In this video I share some very basic things you can ask Fable 5.1 to do, so you can get a feel for how powerful it is.

alt: Video by Roberto P. Nickson on September 01, 2026.

caption:
Why do Japanese companies often manufacture such a wide variety of unrelated products?

I’d always been curious so I decided to dig in.

And well… it’s because their corporate structures prioritize long-term survival and core technical skills over short-term quarterly profits.

Unlike typical Western corporations driven by outside shareholders demanding immediate stock returns, Japanese firms are often managed to keep the company and its workers secure for decades.

This collection of skills and deep expertise compound over time, so these companies can just build whatever the next thing is in-house, instead of spinning off into new companies.

For example, Fujifilm developed such deep process mastery in chemical coatings from camera film to manufacture LCD flat screens and cosmetics.

Now, the American system is best for frontier discovery and innovation.

But, one can make the argument that it’s only so effective because it relies on the slower system.

I also found this interesting:

My friend @nataliefratto just recently shared a video where she argues that this type of corporate culture will soon make its way over to the USA. Check out her video on that.

caption:
Create to serve. I think this message is more relevant now than ever.

Which is why I’m re-uploading one of my most popular videos (with a slightly different intro & sound edit) 

Do you want to build an audience? Ask yourself — what’s in it for them? How can you best serve them?

Is it education? Inspiration? Entertainment?

When you think about it, success is always rooted in service.

When you’re building a startup - any product or service - you’re first identifying what problem you are solving for others.

It’s the same with The Great Online Game.

Creating to serve helps combat burnout too:

When you’re in it for yourself - a certain number or metric - you’re more susceptible to burnout.

When you’re in service to others, there’s a certain strength that comes to you.

&

Fall in love with the journey. You can’t lose.

Astra is currently the world’s most intelligent model, leading across major benchmarks:

98.6% on ARC-AGI-3
97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4
72.6% on OSWorld 2.0 in about 47% less time
73.0% on DeepSWE

While this video is sponsored, everything I mention here is my honest assessment. I encourage you to give Astra your hardest challenge. Something you didn’t think was possible with AI. I think you’ll be surprised.
